patterns: Effective Interview Introduction (60-90 seconds): 1) Name + decade at PIH, 2) Growth trajectory (designer → senior director), 3) Team scope (11 creatives across design/photo/video/archive/web), 4) Two strengths (branding/visual excellence + systems/operations), 5) Concrete example of systems helping development, 6) Personal connection to role/community, 7) Excitement about opportunity. Tested and validated at EBSC Round 2.

Content Gathering Philosophy - 'Go At Their Pace': When getting stories from program staff, emphasize relationship building over quick extraction. Advocate for embedded storytellers within communities vs. flying in from HQ. Shows respect for frontline staff time and addresses common org pain point of development 'bothering' programs too much.

Personal Community Connection as Differentiator: For community-focused roles, leading with authentic personal ties (resident, immigrant background, child in programs) creates immediate rapport and distinguishes from other candidates. Pre-interview casual conversation about shared community (schools, neighborhoods, kids) builds genuine warmth before formal questions begin.

achievementNotes.content: Annual Report as Development Strategy Example: Use annual reports to illustrate proactive content planning—defining chapters, impact stats to measure, stories and photos to gather months in advance rather than scrambling before deadline. Creates flexible content library usable across one-pagers, grants, social media, and ads. Resonates when teams are actively working on annual reports.
